solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stand over fairground's top attraction

definitions.meaning: to straddle, with legs either side
read as two words, the finest ride at a funfair

explanation.surface: A visitor names the most popular thing at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into BEST RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something, legs either side, is to stand over it; split in two it is the finest ride.

clue.text: Cut in half making second separate portion

indicators.note: the second piece separates the portion, splitting it into two parts with itself in between

parts.note: a bit is a portion or piece
sec is a short form of second, a moment of time

explanation.surface: Slicing something down the middle produces a second piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separate' reads as an adjective on portion but is the container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry's word for dividing into two equal parts, from Latin bi- (two) and secare (to cut).

clue.text: Whose sins could produce extravagance?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be reworked to produce something new

explanation.surface: A moralist asks whose wickedness leads to lavish excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentation or flashy display is a kind of extravagance.

clue.text: Take horse round grand crest

indicators.note: the riding word goes round the letter for grand, enclosing it

parts.note: to take horse is to ride
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An instruction to mount up and ride around a great hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the top line of a hill, also called a ridge.

clue.text: Snubbing of French intended

parts.note: de is the French word for of
one's intended is the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.surface: A jilted lover suffers a cold shoulder from a French betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a verb or adjective but is the noun for a betrothed partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Snubbing authority or convention is open defiance, a refusal to comply.

clue.text: Maker of horror films with more overacting

definitions.meaning: ... Films was the British studio famous for Dracula and Frankenstein pictures
a ham is an overacting performer, so a comparative form describes someone hammier still

explanation.surface: A studio boss notes that his horror pictures came with plenty of overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke-comparative of the adjective ham, treated as ham, hammer, hammest.
explanation.definitionFit: The studio name Hammer, and a jokey comparative of ham meaning overacting more.

clue.text: Film nominated for Oscar unanimously by people with judgement finally

parts.note: at one means in agreement, unanimous
men means people

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of judgement

explanation.surface: A jury unanimously picks an Oscar contender.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2007 Joe Wright adaptation of Ian McEwan's novel earned a Best Picture nomination.

clue.text: Island producing whisky of highest grade

parts.note: malt is a type of whisky, single malt
A is the top grade, as in A-grade

explanation.surface: An island known for top-quality whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Settled what you have to do with clue left out

indicators.note: the left-wing word sits on the outside, with the solving word inside it

parts.note: red means left-wing in politics

parts.words: what you have to do with clue
parts.note: one has to solve a crossword clue

explanation.surface: A solver complains that a clue was missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like 'omitted' but splits: 'left' is RED and 'out' says it goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled matter is one that has been decided or sorted out, synonyms in the past participle.

clue.text: Marx got American TV presenter aroused

indicators.note: stirred up or roused, so the letters of the name are shaken into a new order

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey is the famous American chat-show host

explanation.surface: A Marx brother gets an American chat-show host excited.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement is also an exact reversal of OPRAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp-playing, silent one of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: What could produce scared mood — wolf's constant threat

indicators.note: these letters could be reworked to produce a new phrase

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: What makes a wolf frightened? Something always hanging over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Damocles feasted beneath a blade hung by a single hair, an image of ever-present peril.

clue.text: Ringer? A mixed-up creature

parts.note: a chimer is one who rings bells

explanation.surface: Asking whether some confused animal is a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' suggests a double or lookalike; here it is one who rings chimes. 'mixed-up' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek monster with lion, goat and serpent parts is a hybrid beast.

clue.text: Clergyman in vessel to succeed

indicators.note: the clergyman goes in the vessel

parts.note: a pail is a bucket, a vessel for liquid
Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A priest aboard a ship sets out to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: To win through or triumph is to succeed.

clue.text: In place of accused find English Father — punish him?

indicators.note: the English father is found in the dock

parts.note: the dock is where the accused stands in court
Fr is short for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest standing trial in an English court, and should he be punished?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: the 'him' is the Father, and stripping a priest of office is his punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrocking strips a priest of his clerical status as a penalty.

clue.text: Who could make one build marine ark?

definitions.text: Who could make one build marine ark?

indicators.note: the two words could be reworked to make a new word

explanation.surface: Who could bring on a flood bad enough to make someone build a seagoing ark?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings rain could cause a flood like Noah's, which needed an ark.

clue.text: Archbishop once in place of worship

definitions.meaning: William ... was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1940s, and his father Frederick before him
a building for worship, as in a Hindu or Jewish house of prayer

explanation.surface: A former archbishop in a house of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a historical archbishop's surname and a building for religious worship.

clue.text: Pagan term translated as magic symbol

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A heathen word is rendered as an occult sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star used as a charm or occult emblem.

clue.text: Monkey master trained taking little time

indicators.note: the reworked letters take in the short time, holding it inside
trained suggests drilled into shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A monkey whose owner has taught it quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges MASTER into MARSET, which takes in MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American monkey.

clue.text: Old elephant from Burma's to do nothing

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within these words

explanation.surface: An old elephant in Burma is idle.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct elephant-like mammal of the prehistoric era.

clue.text: A Nazi unit to suffer attack

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary unit
to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: A Nazi unit is set to suffer an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault or set upon is to attack, both verbs.

clue.text: Craft displayed in small cocktail

indicators.note: the craft is shown inside the small word

parts.note: mini means small
art means craft or skill

explanation.surface: Skill shown in mixing a little drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail.

clue.text: Open highway of minor importance

definitions.meaning: in Britain a ... is a minor road, below A roads

explanation.surface: An unobstructed minor road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are secondary routes ranked below A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide, open, plain to see; and B-road for a lesser highway.

clue.text: Elaborate screen one used in High Church

indicators.note: to elaborate is to work something out in detail, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An ornate screen used in Anglo-Catholic worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' reads as an adjective on screen but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurible for burning incense, used in ritualist Anglican services.

clue.text: Army man organised military dictatorship

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier sets up a junta.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma, renamed by its ruling junta, was long run by the army.

clue.text: Fruit — one with the makings of meal

parts.note: a means one
meal is ground grain, so corn is what it is made from

explanation.surface: A fruit with ingredients for a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: After big match tucked in with a will

indicators.note: the eating word comes after the match word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: After a big game, the players ate eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' suggests eagerness; it means having left a legal will. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term for someone who dies having made a valid will.

clue.text: Clumsy person Louis Armstrong shunned one time

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so these letters are left out

parts.note: Satchmo was the nickname of the jazz trumpeter
a is one and T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Armstrong once avoided an oaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one time' looks like 'once' but gives A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a stupid or inept fellow, a jerk.

clue.text: Old punishment with blades provides forms of security

parts.note: the stocks held offenders by the ankles for public shaming
and means with
a ploughshare is a plough's blade

explanation.surface: Pillory and blades for securing captives.
explanation.definitionFit: Securities are tradable financial assets such as equities and bonds.

clue.text: Frozen plain fish — doctor tucks in

indicators.note: the doctor is tucked inside the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A doctor eats a frozen plain fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Treeless arctic land with permanently frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Grass court's No.1 after playing well

indicators.note: the royal letters come after the form phrase

parts.note: in form means playing well
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, the first figure at court

explanation.surface: A tennis player's lawn surface after a good game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' and 'court' suggest tennis; Grass is slang for an informant, and ER is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a police informant.
